candidates: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with manubrial invasion
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Previous resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe 12 years ago
Swelling of the manubrium is slightly tender
Swelling increased in size over the month prior to presentation
CT imaging shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium
Lytic lesion is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells
Pathological examination shows thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae
champion: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with manubrial invasion

raw.champion: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with manubrial invasion
raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration and pathological examination showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, along with a history of previous substernal thyroid lobe resection, supports the diagnosis of follicular thyroid carcinoma with local invasion into the manubrium rather than a metastasis.

rejected.label: Metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the direct invasion of thyroid follicles into the manubrium and the history of a previous substernal goiter suggest a local extension or recurrence rather than a distant metastasis.
